docs.title: Taxi-out time prediction at ten European airports
docs.text:
Manuscript

Lamilla Cuellar, J. E., Urbiztondo, M., Parbhakar, A., and Ancheta, C. Recording-Aware Ensembles for Taxi-Out Time Estimation at Ten European Airports. Draft prepared for the Journal of Open Aviation Science; the authors contributed equally. Read the PDF or see the manuscript page for the abstract, sources and build instructions. The draft has not been submitted or peer reviewed and may change, so please do not cite it as a published result.

This site documents team humble-rocket's solution to the PRC Data Challenge 2026: predict the taxi-out time of 670,790 departures at ten European airports in January, February, June and July 2026, trained on all 2025 movements. The metric is RMSE in seconds; February and June were never scored by the daily leaderboard. The code is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later, as the challenge requires.

RMSE (s) Daily leaderboard (January/July half of the submitted file) 221.68 Final ranking <FINAL> 2025 validation, month-held, ex-rollover (2.09 M departures) 191.09 2025 validation, month-held, all rows 227.40

docs.title: The model in one paragraph
docs.text:
A feature matrix built from the challenge movement tables, ADS-B ground tracks (ADSB.lol) and the EUROCONTROL daily ATFM table feeds a set of members built around an explicit model of the off-block stamp: two-stage GBMs that predict the stamp's bounded offset to the flight plan and the probability that it is a schedule-default artifact, distributional transformers whose output histogram is masked to the provable label window, and a class-structured combiner that merges every member's conditional components per recording class (with the team stack as one of its experts). A per-lane simplex blend, fitted month-held on 2025, combines the members; two mechanism-based corrections (feeder-arrival lateness, a 2026 EOBT-filing drift at Paris-CDG) and a set of label-free rules (window clip, rollover identity, twin cap) finish the file. Months are predicted by the member generation whose training-time and test-time inputs are consistent; the final-model page explains why that distinction is worth several seconds of RMSE.

What the label looks like: a morning at Zurich (3 July 2025, drawn from the movement table alone; scripts/animate_taxiout.py rebuilds it). Each bar runs from off-block to take-off. The orange bars carry an off-block stamp copied from the schedule and the grey bars have no flight-plan record: the recording classes the members model separately.

docs.title: Reading guide
docs.text:
The model describes what was built and why:

  • The final submission: the members, the blend, the corrections and rules, and the 2025 results behind the submitted file.
  • Problem and data: what the label actually measures, where the squared error concentrates, and how 2026 differs from 2025.
  • Validation protocol: month-held folds, day-block bootstrap intervals, decision rules calibrated on null comparisons.
  • The team stack: the earlier member stack whose prediction the class-structured combiner consumes as an expert.

Running the code explains the repository and how to reproduce the submission:

  • Reproducing the submission: the whole build in order, from install and data download to the submitted parquet. Start here.
  • Member pipeline: pipeline/, the feature matrix and every trained member.
  • Blend and assembly: final/, the deterministic layer that turns member outputs into the submitted parquet.
  • Package, CLI and scripts: src/prc, the prc command and the post-processing scripts of the team stack.
  • Team stack reproduction: the full rebuild of the team stack from raw data.

Data sources lists every external dataset, its licence and the attribution it asks for. The data itself is never committed; data/README.md in the repository says where to download each file.

docs.title: Reproducing the submission
docs.text:
The full build has nine steps: environment, the challenge data, the external archives, the team stack, its expert table, the feature matrix, the member training, the fold-0 retrains, and the blend and assembly. Every step's commands are on the reproduction page. The last step is deterministic: given the trained member files, it reproduces the submitted parquet byte for byte.

python final/blend.py       # per-lane month-held simplex blend
python final/assemble.py    # corrections + label-free rules -> submissions/humble-rocket_final.parquet
python final/verify.py      # template check, per-month stats, sha256

GPU member training is seeded but not bit-deterministic, so retrained members match ours at seed-noise level; every training run is recorded in pipeline/RUNS.md with its tag, flags and seeds.

docs.title: 1.1 Task
docs.text:
The PRC Data Challenge 2026 asks for the taxi-out time of every departure at ten European airports in January and July 2026, given all 2025 movements as training data.

TAXITIME_SEC_mvt = MVT_TIME_UTC_mvt − BLOCK_TIME_UTC_mvt
                   (take-off)          (off-block, as recorded by the airport)
Airports EDDF, EDDM, EGLL, EHAM, LEBL, LEMD, LFPG, LIRF, LSZH, LTFM Training 2,085,047 departures in 2025 (4.17 M movements incl. arrivals) Ranking set 344,841 departures in January and July 2026 Metric RMSE in seconds over the ranking set

The ranking set contains every field of the departure except the off-block time and the label: take-off time, runway, stand, schedule, aircraft, and the Network Manager (NM) flight-plan fields, including AOBT_3_flt, NM's off-block time. Arrivals in the test months are complete, labels included. The organizers allow all of these fields as inputs.

Two column families matter throughout:

  • _mvt columns come from the airport's movement record. Every departure has them.
  • _flt columns come from the NM flight plan, joined by the organizers. 1.08 % of 2025 departures and 1.53 % of the ranking departures have no flight-plan record; on those rows every _flt column is null. This document calls them the no-flight-plan rows.

docs.title: 1.2 What the label measures
docs.text:
The organizers score the off-block stamp as the airports reported it, without cleaning. The 2025 labels show that this stamp is not always a physical off-block time.

Recording pattern How it shows in the data Frequency in 2025 Schedule default off-block stamp equals the scheduled time within 10 s, so the label equals C = MVT − SCHED 4.80 % of departures; 18.1 % at LIRF Day rollover off-block stamp one day early; label ≈ 86,400 s 15 departures (13 at LIRF) Early stamp label above 1 h on a row with an NM off-block time; in a group of ~630 such rows the airport stamp precedes NM's by a median 3,055 s 0.10 % (2,048 rows) NM proxy on a derived value AOBT_3_flt is take-off minus a per-airport constant (LTFM ≈ 1,200 s and 1,500 s; LIRF ≈ 595 s; EDDM ≈ 300 s; EGLL ≈ 600 s), not a measurement 42 % of LTFM rows in 2025

The arrival records of January and July 2026 carry the same patterns at the same rates (for example LIRF in-block equal to schedule: 8.6 % and 10.6 % in 2026 against 8.7 % and 8.9 % in 2025). The ranking labels therefore contain the same mixture.

Consequence. Under RMSE the best prediction is the conditional mean of the recorded label, not of the physical taxi time. A model has to predict the probability of each recording pattern and the value the label takes under it. Section 2 describes how the model does this.

docs.title: 1.3 Where the error is
docs.text:
Squared error is concentrated in a few rows. Shares of the final model's 2025 out-of-fold squared error (docs/03-validation.md describes the protocol):

Rows Count Share of rows Share of squared error RMSE (s) Day rollovers 15 < 0.01 % 28.8 % 46,534 No flight plan (rollovers excluded) 22,456 1.08 % 15.6 % 887 With flight plan, C ≥ 1 h 179,947 8.63 % 17.0 % 327 With flight plan, C < 1 h, label > 1 h 115 0.01 % 0.4 % 1,901 Everything else 1,882,514 90.29 % 38.2 % 151

C = MVT − SCHED is the delay of the take-off against the schedule. It is known on every test row, and it is the value a schedule-default label takes. Rows with large C carry most of the label mixture.

The 15 rollover rows decide much of any pooled comparison. Every comparison in this repository is therefore reported on all rows and with the rollover rows removed (ex_ro).

docs.title: 1.4 Differences between 2025 and 2026
docs.text: Difference Evidence Effect LIRF has almost no ADS-B ground coverage in July 2026 share of LIRF departures with an ADS-B ground track: 0.956 in July 2025, 0.002 in July 2026 (0.80 in January 2026) members trained with ADS-B features see an input state at LIRF that 2025 barely contains; handled by routing (docs/02-method.md §2.4) EHAM no-flight-plan rate 1.6 % in 2025, 5.0 % in January 2026 more rows in the hardest group LTFM derived-AOBT share 42 % in 2025, 54 % in July 2026 more rows where AOBT_3_flt is not a measurement ADS-B archive gaps in early 2025 the ADSB.lol heatmap files for 2025-01-01 to 2025-04-20 drop ground tracks at EGLL, EDDF and EHAM those 110 days are rebuilt from full traces (docs/05-reproduction.md)

docs.title: 1.5 Data used
docs.text: The challenge tables plus open external sources: ADS-B ground tracks (ADSB.lol), METAR observations (Iowa Environmental Mesonet), Open-Meteo reanalysis, OpenStreetMap aeroway geometry, X-Plane Scenery Gateway stand data and OurAirports runway data. Licences, fetch scripts and attributions: docs/data-sources.md.

docs.text:
challenge data + external archives
        │
        ▼
feature blocks (content-addressed cache)                      §2.2
        │
        ▼
members: CatBoost, RealMLP, GRU, set-attention, TabM          §2.3
  each with a recording-pattern head:  Σ p_k·C_k + (1 − Σ p_k)·ŷ
        │

Every stage after the members is a post-processor. It reads a finished run's out-of-fold and test predictions and writes a new run in the same format, so every stage is scored with the same paired comparison (docs/03-validation.md).

docs.title: 2.2 Features
docs.text:
A feature block is a function of the full movement table (2025 and 2026, departures and arrivals) that returns one row per movement. No block reads the label or the off-block time of the row it describes. Labels enter only through fold-scoped target encodings. Blocks are cached under a hash of their source code, their input and any external archive they read.

Blocks used by every final member:

Block Content Source calendar_v2, cats time of day, weekday, month; airport, runway, stand, operator, aircraft type as categoricals challenge fpl_deltas, fpl_updates take-off minus each flight-plan time (EOBT, AOBT, …) and their pairwise differences challenge regime real NM off-block, derived constant, or no NM record; which derived constant challenge throughput, sched_demand, runway_gaps_v2 rolling take-off and landing counts, scheduled demand, gaps between runway movements challenge surface_queue, discharge_v2, arrival_occupancy_v2 aircraft on the surface at pushback, take-offs and landings during the taxi window, queue position, measured taxi of neighbouring departures challenge arrival_taxi_in rolling taxi-in statistics of recent arrivals challenge stand_bounds_v2 time since the stand's previous departure and arrival: physical bounds on the off-block time challenge source_mismatch, identity_freq, feed_health disagreements between the airport and NM records, carrier and callsign identity, window share of rows without a flight plan challenge metar_visibility, winter_ops visibility, ceiling, low-visibility procedures, frozen precipitation, de-icing likelihood IEM METAR daylight_curfew solar elevation, local hour, minutes to and from night curfew computed adsb_ground from the open ADS-B track: time from first ground movement to take-off, path length, stop time, final hold, ground speed, coverage flags ADSB.lol adsb_ground_v2 where the track starts relative to the stand, stand-to-threshold distance, pushback signature ADSB.lol

Added by some members: taxi_distance (taxiway-graph distance from stand to threshold; OpenStreetMap), stand_xplane (stand size class, type and heading; X-Plane Scenery Gateway), context_sets (the index used by the sequence and set models to gather nearby movements).

Five target encodings (airport × runway, × stand, × stand × runway, × operator, × aircraft type; mean, p10, p50, count) are fitted inside each fold, on clean labels only, with shrinkage.

The ranking set is post-operational: every take-off time is known. Queue and window features therefore use other movements' take-off times on both sides of the row. They never use another departure's off-block time or label.

docs.title: 2.3 Members and the recording-pattern head
docs.text:
Every member predicts on a square-root target and carries the same head. For each recording pattern k with a value C_k that is computable on a test row, a fold-scoped XGBoost classifier estimates p_k. The prediction is the conditional mean:

ŷ = Σ_k p_k · C_k + (1 − Σ_k p_k) · ŷ_normal
Pattern k Training label (from the target, training rows only) Value C_k schedule default |BLOCK − SCHED| ≤ 10 s MVT − SCHED, exactly the label day rollover |y − 86,400| < 3,600 s 86,400 s + ŷ_normal (15 positives; falls back to the base rate) early stamp y > 1 h with an NM record, not one of the above ŷ_normal + 1,495 s (fold-fitted mean offset)

The normal regressor is trained on all rows with sample weight 1 − Σ p_k, where p comes from heads nested inside the training fold.

Final members:

Member Model Notes exp0250 CatBoost (depth 10, lr 0.02, leaf ≥ 100) + taxi_distance, stand_xplane; tail-prone blocks masked on no-flight-plan rows exp0235 CatBoost + the out-of-fold prediction of a GRU member (exp0223), built with three inner groups per fold exp0225 RealMLP + taxi_distance exp0227 / exp0268 RealMLP no masking; exp0268 uses hyper-parameters from a TPE search (§3.6) exp0232 / exp0271 GRU over the airport's movement sequence around the departure exp0271 tuned exp0233 set-attention over nearby movements exp0234 TabM (BatchEnsemble MLP)

The neural members are implemented in plain PyTorch in src/prc/models/ (RealMLP after Holzmüller et al. 2024, TabM after Gorishniy et al. 2025). Each member is trained with three seeds; its test prediction comes from a fit on all twelve 2025 months.

docs.title: 2.4 Routing on ADS-B coverage
docs.text:
Roughly 40 % of departures have no ADS-B ground track: all of LTFM, most of LFPG, and LIRF in July 2026 (docs/01-problem-and-data.md §1.4). A member trained with ADS-B features predicts these rows from a missing-value pattern it has seen rarely at some airports.

For four members a twin is trained without the 21 ADS-B ground columns (exp0259, exp0269, exp0262, exp0263). scripts/route_no_ground.py takes the twin's prediction on rows without a ground track and the base member's elsewhere. The routing flag is label-free.

docs.title: 2.5 Lane head for departures without a flight plan
docs.text:
On no-flight-plan rows every _flt column is null and the member's head loses its strongest inputs. scripts/no_nm_lane_model.py fits a two-branch estimator on these rows only:

ŷ = p̂ · C + (1 − p̂) · ŷ_lane,        C = MVT − SCHED

with LightGBM for p̂ and ŷ_lane, leave-one-month-out. The airports where it replaces the member are chosen inside each fold from the other months only.

docs.title: 2.6 Stamp mixture
docs.text:
scripts/mixture_v2.py models the recorded label of every departure as a mixture of six classes. The classes are training targets derived from the off-block stamp; they are never inputs.

Class Definition Value default |BLOCK − SCHED| ≤ 10 s C far off-block more than 1 h before schedule max(C, 0) + 3600·e^a near C > 30 min and 10 s < |BLOCK − SCHED| ≤ 15 min C − 900·tanh(a) early NM record, label > 1 h (MVT − AOBT_3) + Δ_E(x) block ≪ flight plan NM record, AOBT_3 − BLOCK > 40 min, NM taxi in [0, 1 h] (MVT − AOBT_3) + Δ_B(x) normal the rest ŷ_member · e^a

A PyTorch network outputs the class probabilities and bounded per-row value heads. The loss is the squared error of Σ p_k v_k on the raw scale plus a class log-loss. Classes that cannot occur on a row, by test-observable facts, are masked out of the softmax. Folds are nested leave-one-month-out; the test side is the mean of the thirteen fold models (--test-foldavg), averaged over two seeds. The result is blended with the member's prediction at a fold-selected weight.

docs.title: 2.7 Cell stacker
docs.text:
scripts/stack_l2.py --family cell combines the seven members with non-negative weights that sum to one, per cell of airport × flight-plan record present × C band (< 30 min, 30-60 min, 1-2 h,

2 h). Cell weights are shrunk toward their parent (flight-plan record × band, then global); the shrinkage strength is chosen by inner leave-one-month-out. Rollover rows are excluded from every fit. The test-side combiner is fitted on all twelve months.

Global weights of the final stack:

Member (after lane head and mixture) Weight routed GRU (exp0271 / exp0262) 0.445 routed RealMLP (exp0268 / exp0269) 0.309 routed set-attention (exp0233 / exp0263) 0.148 routed CatBoost (exp0250 / exp0259) 0.098 CatBoost + GRU stack (exp0235) 0.000 RealMLP + taxi distance (exp0225) 0.000 TabM (exp0234) 0.000

Members with zero global weight still carry weight in some cells.

docs.title: 2.8 Gate on C
docs.text:
scripts/gate_runs.py takes the final stack on rows with C < 1 h (87.5 % of test rows) and an earlier stack on the rest. The earlier stack has the same structure with the unrouted members (exp0250, exp0235, exp0225, exp0227, exp0232, exp0233, exp0234) and one mixture fit each.

The reason: on 2025 validation, rows with C ≥ 1 h (rollovers excluded) score 398.0 with the earlier stack and 400.3-400.8 with the later ones. In 2026 those rows include a population with no 2025 counterpart: LIRF in July 2026, delayed, without ADS-B ground coverage. Changes that moved these rows could not be validated, so the final model leaves them on the earlier stack.

docs.title: 3. Validation
docs.text: The public leaderboard scores one fixed set of 344,841 rows. Its result was used only to check whole models. Every decision about a component was made on 2025 data, with the rules below written before the run.

docs.title: 3.1 Folds
docs.text:
Scheme Training Validation Use month_loo 11 months of 2025 the held-out month; 12 folds main estimate: every 2025 row gets one out-of-fold prediction tail_nov_dec January to October 2025 November and December 2025 forward check: training strictly before validation month_jan_jul 2025 without January and July January and July 2025 early development and screening; the two months the test months correspond to

Random K-fold splits are never used as evidence: they leak within-month conditions (weather, runway configuration, recording behaviour) between training and validation.

Post-processors (lane head, mixture, stacker) are fitted leave-one-month-out on the members' out-of-fold predictions, with their own hyper-parameters chosen inside the training months. Their test-side models are fitted on all twelve months.

docs.title: 3.2 Paired comparisons
docs.text:
A change is always compared against a twin: the same configuration without the change, same seeds, same folds. scripts/paired_delta.py reports the RMSE difference on each row group.

Intervals come from a day-block bootstrap: blocks are airport × UTC date, resampled within airport-month, 2,000 replicates. Errors within a day are strongly correlated (weather, runway configuration, one bad recording day at one airport). The spread between seeds understates the uncertainty by a factor of 10 to 100 and is not used as an interval.

Every comparison is reported on:

Row group Why all the objective ex_ro all rows without the 15 day rollovers, which hold 29 % of the final model's squared error January, July (ex_ro) the seasons of the two test months each month consistency: how many of 12 months improve ordinary rows with a flight-plan record, off the derived-AOBT value, label ≤ 1 h no flight plan the rows with the largest per-row error C < 1 h, C ≥ 1 h label-free split on delay against schedule (docs/01-problem-and-data.md §1.3) each airport no airport may lose more than 5 s without a stated reason

docs.title: 3.3 Decision rules
docs.text:
Each experiment declares its class in its configuration before it runs. The class fixes the number it is judged on; it is not changed after the result is visible.

Class What it changes Adopted when ordinary features, encodings, hyper-parameters, members ex_ro interval below zero; January and July not worse (point estimate ≤ +0.5 s, interval not wholly above zero); ≥ 8 of 12 months better; forward check not worse tail anything that moves under 1 % of rows by more than 1,000 s all interval below zero; the ex_ro cost stated in advance and not exceeded; expected effect on the test set computed from a shrunk incidence prior, with a bounded loss if the pattern does not occur combination member set, stack weights nested fit; all-row and ex_ro reported for the year, January and July

A gain concentrated in fewer than 100 rows is treated as a tail change. A new feature block must also pass a drift check: no column shifts by more than 0.25 standard deviations between 2025 and 2026 January/July without an explanation.

docs.title: 3.4 How often the rule accepts noise
docs.text:
The rule was calibrated on null comparisons (A/A tests): pairs that differ only by seed, and pairs of identical mixture fits that differ only by random initialisation.

Null source Comparisons Accepted by "point estimate < 0 and ≥ 7 of 12 months" Accepted by "interval below zero" member seeds 60 37 % 7 % mixture refits 20 35 % 5 %

A point-estimate rule accepts about a third of null changes. The interval rule accepts 5 to 7 %. All decisions use the interval.

docs.title: 3.5 Confirmation and the winner's curse
docs.text: When several variants are screened and the best is kept, its screened gain is biased upward. A variant chosen on one seed is therefore re-run with fresh seeds, and only the fresh-seed result counts. Example from one selection round: a mixture setting chosen from a grid improved one member on C ≥ 1 h rows by 3.76 s [−6.95, −1.00]; with fresh seeds, across all seven members and through the stacker, it was 2.32 s worse [−0.37, +5.20] than the final model on those rows. It was not adopted.

docs.title: 3.6 Hyper-parameter search
docs.text: Hyper-parameters were searched only where a twin comparison could confirm the result. The search (Optuna TPE) ran on January and July 2025 with one seed and the member's ordinary-row RMSE as the objective. The selected configuration was then run on month_loo with three new seeds and judged on the ten months the search never saw. Two searches passed this (RealMLP exp0268, GRU exp0271); the set-attention search did not.

docs.title: 3.7 Changes to the input archives
docs.text: The ADS-B archive for 2025-01-01 to 2025-04-20 was rebuilt from full traces partway through the work (docs/05-reproduction.md). For a comparison between members trained on the two archive states, the validation features of January to April differ between the two sides. Such comparisons are read on May to December 2025 only, where the evaluated rows are byte-identical.

docs.title: 3.8 Validation and the test set
docs.text: The leaderboard result was used as a check on whole candidate models. Component decisions were made on 2025 data. 2025 validation tracks the leaderboard closely for rows with C < 1 h. It does not cover one 2026 population: delayed LIRF departures in July 2026 without ADS-B ground coverage. This is why the final model is gated on C (docs/02-method.md §2.8).

docs.title: 5. Reproduction
docs.text: This document rebuilds the final submission from the raw challenge data. Every command runs from the repository root. GPU steps are given twice where it matters: as a SLURM job (jobs/slurm/) and as a plain command for a machine with one GPU.

docs.title: 5.1 The chain
docs.text:
challenge data ─ prepare ─┐
external archives ────────┼─ feature cache (ADS-B state H) ─ H members ─┐
                          │                                             │
                          ├─ routing flag (state H)                     │
                          └─ traces rebuild of 2025-01-01..04-20 (state T) ─ T members
                                                                        │
      routing ── lane heads ── mixture v2 ── two cell stacks ── gate ── candidate file

The final prediction is a gate of two stacks on C = MVT − SCHED (label-free, known for every row):

rows stack members (each: lane head, then mixture v2) C < 1 h stack_l2_cell_ng4h2G route_ng, exp0235, exp0225, route_ngRh2, route_ngGh, route_ngS, exp0234; mixture averaged over two fold-averaged fits (_mx2faA) C ≥ 1 h stack_l2_cell_mx2_xp exp0250, exp0235, exp0225, exp0227, exp0232, exp0233, exp0234; one mixture fit each (_mx2)

A routed member route_<tag> takes a no-ADS-B expert's prediction on rows without an ADS-B ground track and the base member's prediction elsewhere:

routed member base no-ADS-B expert route_ng exp0250_r7d_cat_sqrt_taxi_distance_xplane (H) exp0259_r7d_cat_sqrt_taxi_distance_xplane_noadsb (T) route_ngRh2 exp0268_r7c_realmlp_nomask_adsbtr_hp1 (T) exp0269_r7c_realmlp_nomask_noadsb_hp1 (T) route_ngGh exp0271_r7c_seqenc_slog_nomask_adsbtr_hp1 (T) exp0262_r7c_seqenc_slog_nomask_noadsb (T) route_ngS exp0233_r7c_setenc_slog_nomask (H) exp0263_r7c_setenc_slog_nomask_noadsb (T)

exp0235_r7d_cat_stack_gru is a CatBoost member with one extra input: the out-of-fold prediction of the GRU member exp0223_r7c_seqenc_slog. It needs 39 inner GRU runs (§5.8).

Two ADS-B archive states. The ADSB.lol heatmap files of 2025-01-01 to 2025-04-20 drop ground tracks at EGLL, EDDF and EHAM. Those 110 days are rebuilt from the full traces. Members marked H were trained on the heatmap archive, members marked T on the rebuilt one. Only those 110 days differ; every other 2025 day and every 2026 day is identical in both states. An exact rebuild therefore trains the H members, writes the routing flag, rebuilds the 110 days, and then trains the T members.

docs.title: 5.2 Requirements
docs.text:
GPU steps ran on NVIDIA L40S cards with 48 GB of memory, one card per array task. The SLURM templates request the CPU cores and RAM below; set the time limit for your cluster.

step resource ADS-B heatmap build (§5.5) CPU; internet access, about 550 GB streamed; 9 GB transient disk member cells, H and T (§5.8, §5.11) 1 CUDA GPU with 48 GB per seed; 8 CPU cores, 80 GB RAM exp0223 inner runs (§5.8) 1 CUDA GPU with 48 GB per task, 39 tasks; 16 CPU cores, 160 GB RAM stack table (§5.8) CPU; 4 cores, 16 GB RAM traces rebuild (§5.10) 11 CPU tasks; internet access; 12 GB RAM and up to 9 GB transient disk per task mixture v2 fits (§5.13) 1 CUDA GPU with 48 GB per fit, 21 fits; 8 CPU cores, 64 GB RAM routing, lane heads, applies, stacks, gate, candidate CPU; up to 32 GB RAM

Disk: raw and interim challenge data 0.6 GB, feature cache 1.8 GB, external archives 3.1 GB, about 0.1 GB per run directory.

docs.title: 5.3 Environment
docs.text:
git clone <repository URL> && cd prc-data-challenge-2026-humble-rocket
uv sync --group nn          # Python 3.12 and the locked packages, PyTorch included

uv installs Python 3.12 if it is missing. uv.lock pins every package (PyTorch 2.14, XGBoost 3.4.1, CatBoost 1.2.10). The GPU driver must support the CUDA version of the locked PyTorch wheels. Every GPU job script checks for a visible GPU before it starts.

On a SLURM cluster, enable the ##SBATCH --account, --partition and --time lines of the templates in jobs/slurm/ for your site and create the log directory once: mkdir -p jobs/logs.

docs.title: 5.4 Challenge data
docs.text:
The organizers issue access keys to registered teams. Keys never go into a file in the repository.

mc alias set prc https://s3.opensky-network.org <access-key> <secret-key>   # MinIO client, once
cp .env.example .env              # set PRC_TEAM_NAME; PRC_DATA_BUCKET is the organizers' bucket
uv run prc data pull              # mc mirror -> data/raw/
uv run prc data prepare           # -> data/interim/movements.parquet

jobs/slurm/stage-data.sbatch runs the same steps plus the feature build of §5.6. data/raw/manifest.json records the sha256 of every challenge file, so a reissued file is visible.

docs.title: 5.5 External archives (state H)
docs.text:
Sources, licences and attributions: docs/data-sources.md. Run these on a CPU node with internet access.

uv run python scripts/fetch_external.py ourairports   # first: the ADS-B build reads runway thresholds
uv run python scripts/fetch_external.py metar --years 2025 2026
uv run python scripts/fetch_external.py osm           # -> data/external/osm_<date>/
uv run python scripts/fetch_external.py xplane        # -> data/external/xplane_gateway_<date>/
uv run python scripts/fetch_external.py openmeteo     # read by the mixture v2 frame
uv run python scripts/adsb_build.py run --stage 1 --workers 3   # 2025-01, 2025-07, 2026-01, 2026-07
uv run python scripts/adsb_build.py run --stage 2 --workers 3   # the other ten 2025 months

adsb_build.py reads the heatmap files and falls back to the full traces for a day without them. It resumes where it stopped. Keep exactly one data/external/osm_* directory: the taxi_distance block reads the lexically last one.

docs.title: 5.6 Feature cache (state H)
docs.text:
uv run prc features build --all

Run it after §5.5. The cache is content-addressed (data/features/<block>__<source hash>__<input hash>[__x<external hash>].parquet), so the H and T caches of the ADS-B blocks live side by side.

docs.title: 5.7 Running one member cell
docs.text:
A member is one experiment YAML in experiments/, run with three seeds. Each seed is one cell: every fold of the CV scheme, plus (with test_fit: full in the YAML) one fit on all of 2025 that writes the test prediction.

With SLURM, one array task per seed:

cell() {  # cell <experiment> <scheme> <run root> [seeds]
  local seeds="${4:-1,2,3}"
  CONFIG="experiments/$1.yaml" SCHEME="$2" OUT_ROOT="outputs/runs/$3" SEEDS="$seeds" \
    sbatch --parsable --array=0-2 --export=ALL,CONFIG,SCHEME,OUT_ROOT,SEEDS \
    jobs/slurm/member-cell.sbatch
}
cell exp0225_r7c_realmlp_taxi month_loo loo-exp0225_r7c_realmlp_taxi

Without SLURM, on one GPU, the same cells one after another:

e=exp0225_r7c_realmlp_taxi
for s in 1 2 3; do
  uv run python scripts/run_cell.py --config "experiments/$e.yaml" --seed "$s" \
    --scheme month_loo --out "outputs/runs/loo-$e"
done

Each cell writes outputs/runs/loo-<exp>/<exp>__s<seed>__month_loo/. A cell whose metrics.json exists is skipped, so a rerun resumes.

Check every cell before merging. A cell can finish with a NaN fold; that fold's rows are then missing from its out-of-fold file.

for s in outputs/runs/loo-*/*/status.json; do
  uv run python -c "import json, math, sys; d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); \
bad = [i for i, x in enumerate(d['fit_rmse']) if x is None or math.isnan(x)]; \
print(sys.argv[1], 'NaN folds', bad) if bad else None" "$s"
done

Rerun a member with a NaN fold with the next unused seed (SEEDS=4), drop the failed cell's directory from the run root, and merge.

Merge the seeds into one run directory per member:

uv run python scripts/merge_seeds.py merge-seeds outputs/runs/loo-exp0225_r7c_realmlp_taxi
# -> outputs/runs/exp0225_r7c_realmlp_taxi__s1-2-3__month_loo/

The merge joins the cells on the movement id, refuses cells of different configs or rows, and recomputes every metric. The merged name carries the seeds (__s2-3-4__ for seeds 2, 3, 4).

docs.title: 5.8 H members
docs.text:
Train on the heatmap archive (state H), before §5.10.

for e in exp0250_r7d_cat_sqrt_taxi_distance_xplane exp0225_r7c_realmlp_taxi \
         exp0227_r7c_realmlp_nomask exp0232_r7c_seqenc_slog_nomask \
         exp0233_r7c_setenc_slog_nomask exp0234_r7c_tabm_slog_nomask exp0223_r7c_seqenc_slog; do
  cell "$e" month_loo "loo-$e"
done
cell exp0223_r7c_seqenc_slog tail_nov_dec fwd-exp0223_r7c_seqenc_slog

Then the stacked member exp0235. Its stack table needs 39 inner runs of exp0223 (3 seeds × the 13 outer training-month sets of month_loo and tail_nov_dec) and the two exp0223 run roots above:

MEMBER=exp0223_r7c_seqenc_slog OUT_ROOT=outputs/runs/inner-exp0223_r7c_seqenc_slog \
  sbatch --array=0-38%8 --export=ALL,MEMBER,OUT_ROOT jobs/slurm/stack-inner.sbatch
sbatch jobs/slurm/stack-build.sbatch           # after the inner runs and both exp0223 roots
cell exp0235_r7d_cat_stack_gru month_loo loo-exp0235_r7d_cat_stack_gru

Without SLURM: uv run python scripts/stack_inner.py inner --member exp0223_r7c_seqenc_slog --out outputs/runs/inner-exp0223_r7c_seqenc_slog runs all 39 inner runs in sequence; scripts/stack_inner.py build (arguments in the script's docstring and in jobs/slurm/stack-build.sbatch) writes the table to data/stack/exp0223_r7c_seqenc_slog__g3/.

Check the cells (§5.7), then merge the seven member roots:

for r in outputs/runs/loo-exp02{25,27,32,33,34,35,50}_*; do
  uv run python scripts/merge_seeds.py merge-seeds "$r"
done

docs.title: 5.9 Routing flag (state H)
docs.text:
Write the flag before the traces rebuild, while data/external/ holds the heatmap archive:

uv run python scripts/write_route_flag.py exp0250_r7d_cat_sqrt_taxi_distance_xplane__s1-2-3__month_loo
# -> outputs/route/adsb_has_gnd_heatmap.parquet

Our flag: 2,429,888 rows; 1,444,508 with a ground track, 980,665 without, 4,715 null (null is routed as "no ground track").

docs.title: 5.10 Traces rebuild (state T)
docs.text:
P=$(MODE=prep sbatch --parsable --export=ALL,MODE jobs/slurm/adsb-traces.sbatch)
Q=$(MODE=pull sbatch --parsable --dependency=afterok:$P --array=0-10%8 --export=ALL,MODE jobs/slurm/adsb-traces.sbatch)
MODE=v2 sbatch --dependency=afterok:$Q --export=ALL,MODE jobs/slurm/adsb-traces.sbatch

prep keeps a backup of the 110 heatmap days. pull rebuilds 10 days per task from the full traces. v2 checks that all 110 days were rebuilt, rebuilds their v2 archive and the adsb_ground / adsb_ground_v2 feature cache. Without SLURM, run the three modes in order with bash, setting SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID=0 to 10 for pull.

docs.title: 5.11 T members
docs.text:
Train after §5.10. Our exp0269 seed-1 cell diverged, so that member uses seeds 2, 3 and 4.

for e in exp0259_r7d_cat_sqrt_taxi_distance_xplane_noadsb exp0262_r7c_seqenc_slog_nomask_noadsb \
         exp0263_r7c_setenc_slog_nomask_noadsb exp0268_r7c_realmlp_nomask_adsbtr_hp1 \
         exp0271_r7c_seqenc_slog_nomask_adsbtr_hp1; do
  cell "$e" month_loo "loo-$e"
done
cell exp0269_r7c_realmlp_nomask_noadsb_hp1 month_loo loo-exp0269_r7c_realmlp_nomask_noadsb_hp1 2,3,4

Check the cells (§5.7), then merge:

for r in outputs/runs/loo-exp02{59,62,63,68,69,71}_*; do
  uv run python scripts/merge_seeds.py merge-seeds "$r"
done

docs.title: 5.12 Routing and lane heads
docs.text:
CPU only.

F=outputs/route/adsb_has_gnd_heatmap.parquet
L=__s1-2-3__month_loo
uv run python scripts/route_no_ground.py exp0250_r7d_cat_sqrt_taxi_distance_xplane$L \
  exp0259_r7d_cat_sqrt_taxi_distance_xplane_noadsb$L route_ng__month_loo --flag $F
uv run python scripts/route_no_ground.py exp0268_r7c_realmlp_nomask_adsbtr_hp1$L \
  exp0269_r7c_realmlp_nomask_noadsb_hp1__s2-3-4__month_loo route_ngRh2__month_loo --flag $F
uv run python scripts/route_no_ground.py exp0271_r7c_seqenc_slog_nomask_adsbtr_hp1$L \
  exp0262_r7c_seqenc_slog_nomask_noadsb$L route_ngGh__month_loo --flag $F
uv run python scripts/route_no_ground.py exp0233_r7c_setenc_slog_nomask$L \
  exp0263_r7c_setenc_slog_nomask_noadsb$L route_ngS__month_loo --flag $F

The expert's seed columns fill the base's seed slots by position, so the s2-3-4 expert routes into an s1-2-3 base.

Lane head on departures without a flight-plan record, 11 runs:

lane() {  # lane <source run> <name> -> outputs/runs/<name>_lane
  uv run python scripts/no_nm_lane_model.py fit --run "$1" --out "outputs/lane/$2.parquet"
  uv run python scripts/no_nm_lane_model.py apply --run "$1" --lane "outputs/lane/$2.parquet" \
    --out "$2_lane" --auto-airports
}
for e in exp0250_r7d_cat_sqrt_taxi_distance_xplane exp0235_r7d_cat_stack_gru exp0225_r7c_realmlp_taxi \
         exp0227_r7c_realmlp_nomask exp0232_r7c_seqenc_slog_nomask exp0233_r7c_setenc_slog_nomask \
         exp0234_r7c_tabm_slog_nomask; do
  lane "$e$L" "$e"
done
for t in ng ngRh2 ngGh ngS; do lane "route_${t}__month_loo" "route_$t"; done

--auto-airports chooses the airports where the lane head replaces the member, fold-safe.

docs.title: 5.13 Mixture v2
docs.text:
The member-independent frame once, then one GPU fit per lane run. The fit settings are fixed in jobs/slurm/mixture-v2.sbatch (--device cuda --batch 4096 --lr 2e-3 --epochs 40 --patience 5 --n-seeds 8).

V15=exp0250_r7d_cat_sqrt_taxi_distance_xplane_lane,exp0235_r7d_cat_stack_gru_lane,exp0225_r7c_realmlp_taxi_lane,exp0227_r7c_realmlp_nomask_lane,exp0232_r7c_seqenc_slog_nomask_lane,exp0233_r7c_setenc_slog_nomask_lane,exp0234_r7c_tabm_slog_nomask_lane
FIN=route_ng_lane,exp0235_r7d_cat_stack_gru_lane,exp0225_r7c_realmlp_taxi_lane,route_ngRh2_lane,route_ngGh_lane,route_ngS_lane,exp0234_r7c_tabm_slog_nomask_lane

J=$(MODE=build sbatch --parsable --export=ALL,MODE jobs/slurm/mixture-v2.sbatch)
# C >= 1 h stack: one full fit per member, seed 0  -> outputs/mixture_v2/<run>__v2.parquet
RUNS=$V15 sbatch --dependency=afterok:$J --array=0-6 --export=ALL,RUNS jobs/slurm/mixture-v2.sbatch
# C < 1 h stack: two fold-averaged fits per member -> <run>__v2__fa0, <run>__v2__fa1
RUNS=$FIN TAG=fa0 MX_ARGS=--test-foldavg \
  sbatch --dependency=afterok:$J --array=0-6 --export=ALL,RUNS,TAG,MX_ARGS jobs/slurm/mixture-v2.sbatch
RUNS=$FIN TAG=fa1 MX_ARGS="--test-foldavg --seed 1" \
  sbatch --dependency=afterok:$J --array=0-6 --export=ALL,RUNS,TAG,MX_ARGS jobs/slurm/mixture-v2.sbatch

Without SLURM: uv run python scripts/mixture_v2.py build --audit, then for each run uv run python scripts/mixture_v2.py fit --run <run> --device cuda --batch 4096 --lr 2e-3 --epochs 40 --patience 5 --n-seeds 8 with --tag fa0 --test-foldavg or --tag fa1 --test-foldavg --seed 1 for the C < 1 h members.

Apply (CPU):

for m in ${V15//,/ }; do uv run python scripts/mixture_v2.py apply --run "$m" --out "${m}_mx2"; done
for m in ${FIN//,/ }; do
  for t in fa0 fa1; do uv run python scripts/mixture_v2.py apply --run "$m" --tag "$t" --out "${m}_mx2$t"; done
  uv run python scripts/avg_runs.py "${m}_mx2fa0" "${m}_mx2fa1" "${m}_mx2faA"
done

docs.title: 5.14 Stacks and gate
docs.text:
uv run python scripts/stack_l2.py $(for m in ${V15//,/ }; do echo "${m}_mx2"; done) \
  --family cell --out stack_l2_cell_mx2_xp
uv run python scripts/stack_l2.py $(for m in ${FIN//,/ }; do echo "${m}_mx2faA"; done) \
  --family cell --out stack_l2_cell_ng4h2G
uv run python scripts/gate_runs.py stack_l2_cell_mx2_xp stack_l2_cell_ng4h2G stack_l2_cell_ng4h2G_lt1h

gate_runs.py takes the second run on rows with C < 3,600 s and the first elsewhere. It reads C from outputs/mixture_v2/exp0227_r7c_realmlp_nomask_lane__v2.parquet (written in §5.13). Member order changes only the log.

docs.title: 5.15 Candidate file and checks
docs.text:
mkdir -p submissions/candidates
uv run python scripts/write_candidate.py stack_l2_cell_ng4h2G_lt1h \
  submissions/candidates/stack_l2_cell_ng4h2G_lt1h_candidate.parquet

write_candidate.py joins the test predictions to the organizers' submission template, clips at 0, rounds to the template's integer type and validates: the two columns, the template's 344,841 ids, no duplicates, no nulls, no non-finite or negative values.

docs.title: 5.16 What "reproduced" means
docs.text:
• GPU training is seeded but not bit-deterministic. A rebuild is not byte-identical to our file.
  • Measured on our runs: two mixture v2 fits of the same member with different seeds differ by about 14 s rmsd on the test rows, even with fold averaging. A full rebuild differs from our submission by an rmsd of that order, with a mean shift under 1 s.
  • The gate structure does not change: rows with C ≥ 1 h come from the stack_l2_cell_mx2_xp stack, rows with C < 1 h from stack_l2_cell_ng4h2G.
  • Out-of-fold scores of the C < 1 h stack should fall within seed noise of ours: RMSE 230.21 s on all 2025 rows, 196.98 s without the 15 day-rollover rows.
  • The CPU steps (routing, lane heads, applies, averaging, stacks, gate, candidate) are deterministic given their inputs: reruns of these steps on our inputs gave sha256-identical outputs.

docs.title: The final submission
docs.text: This document describes the model behind humble-rocket_final.parquet: predictions for the 670,790 departures of final_ranking.parquet (January, February, June and July 2026). It sits on top of the stack documented in docs/01-docs/05: the members here are trained on a compact matrix of raw-derived features plus the ADS-B ground-track columns, and the class model additionally consumes the team stack's prediction (docs/02-method.md) as one of its experts. pipeline/RUNS.md records every training run; final/ holds the blend and assembly code.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Predict the taxi-out time (take-off minus off-block, seconds) of each 2026 departure at ten European airports, trained on twelve labelled months of 2025. Scoring is RMSE. February and June were never on the daily leaderboard; the arrivals of all four months are labelled, the departures are not.

docs.title: What the data taught us
docs.text:
Three properties of the data shape the design.

The join window. The organizers attached an NM flight plan to a departure only when the airport's off-block stamp lay within 3,606 s of the NM system's last off-block time (LOBT). We verified this on all 2,062,577 NM departures of 2025: max |BLOCK − LOBT| is exactly 3,606 s. Two consequences follow.

  1. On every NM row the label provably lies in [MVT − LOBT − 3606, MVT − LOBT + 3606]. Projecting a prediction onto that interval can only reduce its error, so the window clip is the last step of the pipeline, and the strongest members build the bound into their architecture.
  2. "No flight plan" is partly a label-selected event: the join failed because the stamp was far from LOBT. The no-NM lane (about 1 % of rows, roughly a third of the squared error) has a different label distribution and gets its own specialists and blend cells.

Schedule defaults. A recording artifact sets the off-block stamp equal to the scheduled time on a few percent of rows, which makes the label exactly C = MVT − SCHED. Whether a row is a default is driven by operator recording practice, which arrivals reveal without touching any departure label. Most members model P(default) explicitly and predict a mixture.

Lane structure. Error concentrates in a few row populations: no-NM rows, NM rows with long delays, and LIRF. Members are combined per lane rather than globally.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
Trained by the scripts in pipeline/, thirteen folds each: folds 1-12 hold out one 2025 month (the member's honest out-of-fold prediction of it), fold 0 trains on all of 2025 and predicts the evaluation rows.

  • Two-stage GBM (gbm_nested.py): stage 1 predicts properties of the off-block stamp (the bounded offset d = BLOCK − LOBT and its quantiles, P(default), P(long)) with inner month-held folds, so no stage-2 training row sees an in-fold stage-1 fit. Stage 2 fits the taxi time, including the mixture y_mix = p_def · C + (1 − p_def) · normal-model. Variants: a CatBoost mixture, a per-airport mixture, and a four-class stamp specialist (normal / default / near-default / long) that sees the other members' disagreement as features and combines class-specific value models by expectation.
  • Distributional FT-transformer (ftdist.py): a feature-token transformer whose head is a softmax over taxi-time bins masked to the NM join window, plus a point mass at y = C masked where a default is infeasible. The prediction is the distribution mean. Variants: base (7 seeds), stage-1 tokens, strike-calendar tokens, EOBT-free (18 seeds), no-NM rows upweighted.
  • Class-structured combiner (class_mix.py), the strongest single member: y = p_def · C + p_near · (C − offset) + p_long · v_long + p_normal · Σ g_j n_j, where the class probabilities, the gate g over the members' conditional normal means n_j, and small corrections come from one MLP that sees every member's class signals (including the team stack's prediction). A second instance is trained on the no-NM rows only.

docs.title: Two member generations
docs.text:
The challenge released its evaluation data twice: ranking.parquet (the January/July rows scored by the daily leaderboard) first, and final_ranking.parquet (all four months; the same January/July flights with the take-off stamp dithered by a few seconds) close to the deadline. That timing leaves two member generations:

  • the primary members above, whose fold 0 predicts the January/July rows. Each produced its thirteen folds in one nested run, so its out-of-fold behaviour is a faithful proxy for its fold-0 behaviour;
  • fold-0 retrains on the final matrix for the months the primary members never predicted (February/June).

The retrains are one-off fold-0 fits, and that costs them something the 2025 validation cannot see: a stacked model's test-time inputs must come from the same model instances that generated its training inputs. Two retrained members break that symmetry on the final rows: the anomaly specialist's member-deviation features exist only for the January/July rows (its February/ June means collapse by ~500 s against every sibling member), and the class model consumed it as an expert (a 35-65 s depression against its siblings on exactly those two months, within ±10 s elsewhere). Both are therefore excluded from the February/June member lists; everything else about the two generations is identical. January/July rows are predicted by the primary members (their prediction maps to the re-released rows by adding the published take-off-stamp shift, which moves the label by exactly that amount).

docs.title: Blend
docs.text: Per lane (NM C < 1 h, NM C ≥ 1 h, no-NM LIRF, no-NM elsewhere): non-negative least squares on the simplex, lightly shrunk toward equal weights, fitted on the members' month-held 2025 out-of-fold predictions (final/blend.py). Weights scored on month k are fitted on the other eleven, so the February and June rows of the 2025 read are leave-that-month-out estimates, the honest stand-in for the never-evaluated months. On the NM lanes the class combiner carries most of the weight (0.98 / 0.82); the no-NM lanes are led by the transformer variants, and LIRF no-NM by the no-NM class specialist (0.75).

docs.title: Corrections (final/assemble.py)
docs.text:
• Feeder lateness. When the stand's feeding arrival went in-block more than 90 min behind schedule, the blend overshoots slightly (the aircraft tends to leave quickly once ready). Offsets per C band are fitted on the 2025 out-of-fold blend with a heavy smoothing prior and validated month-held (better in 8 of 12 months, interval below zero). Arrival block times are published for the submission months, so the trigger is computable on every 2026 row.
  • LFPG EOBT drift. In June and July 2026 the filed EOBT at LFPG sits about four minutes later relative to LOBT than in any 2025 month; no other airport-month moves comparably. This is a filing-practice change no 2025-trained model has seen, and EOBT-anchored features mis-read exactly those rows. The EOBT-free transformer is immune by construction, so the mean gap between it and the base transformer over the affected cell (LFPG, NM, C < 1 h) estimates the induced bias and is added back there: +17 s in July, +16 s in June. Label-free: the drift is visible in published feature columns, and the magnitude comes from comparing two of our own models.

docs.title: Rules (label-free, proven on 2025)
docs.text:
1. window clip (a projection, so it can only help);
  2. rollover identity: when MVT − LOBT > 20 h, LOBT kept the previous day's date and the label equals MVT − LOBT itself;
  3. twin cap: a no-NM departure whose arrival "twin" (same callsign and route, landing at another challenge airport within six hours) carries an NM plan must have fallen outside the join window, so y ≤ MVT − twin LOBT − 3606. On 2025, labels respect this bound on 810 of 812 twin rows with margin ≥ 300 s;
  4. floor at zero, round, Int32.

docs.title: Validation and results
docs.text:
Everything is selected on 2025 with months held out; candidate changes were accepted on day-block bootstrap intervals of the paired RMSE delta together with counts of months improved, never on a single pooled number (the protocol of docs/03-validation.md). Rollover rows are excluded from member training and reported separately, because three or four rows a year would otherwise dominate any comparison.

2025 month-held reads of the delivered construction, ex-rollover (results/blend_report.txt):

read RMSE (s) all twelve months 191.09 lane NM C < 1 h 149.37 lane NM C ≥ 1 h 310.58 lane no-NM other 588.53 lane no-NM LIRF 2538.10 February (leave-out, retrain member list) 200.87 June (leave-out, retrain member list) 201.78

The daily leaderboard (January/July 2026 only) scored this file's January/July half at 221.68. The leaderboard was used as a deployment sanity check of completed submissions; the pipeline incorporates no leaderboard-derived values, and its one 2026-specific term (the LFPG adjustment) is estimated label-free as described above.

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text: Taxi-out time, the interval between an aircraft leaving its stand and taking off, drives fuel burn on the ground and enters the take-off times on which network planning relies. Many estimation studies treat the recorded off-block time as a physical event and validate on random splits of short, single-airport samples. For 2,085,047 departures at ten large European airports in 2025, we show that the recorded label has exploitable structure. Flight-plan records appear to have been attached to movements only when the recorded off-block stamp lay within 3,606 s of the last flight-plan off-block time, a tolerance we infer from the data, so every matched departure carries a provable interval for its label, and a missing flight plan is itself informative. Off-block stamps coincide with the scheduled time on 4.8% of departures; at one airport (Rome Fiumicino) this happens on 18.1% of departures against 2.5% one minute either side, which indicates a recording artefact. Because the error measure is computed on the recorded label, we model it as a mixture of recording classes. The members are two-stage gradient-boosted trees, a distributional transformer whose histogram is masked to the feasible interval, and a class-structured combiner whose experts include an earlier stack of tabular, sequence and set models. A per-lane non-negative blend and label-free projections complete the estimator. Components are selected with month-held, nested cross-validation and, for ordinary changes, day-block bootstrap intervals under decision rules calibrated by null comparisons. On held-out months of 2025 the blend reaches an RMSE of 191.1 s (95% interval 183.5 to 201.7 s) when 15 day-rollover records are excluded, and 227.4 s on all records. Error concentrates in departures without a flight plan and long delays. We also describe a label-free check for input drift and a consistency requirement for the inputs of stacked models.

The LaTeX source lives in the repository's manuscript/ folder, in the journal's template format:

docs.title: Reproducing the submission
docs.text:
This page runs the whole build in order, from a fresh clone to submissions/humble-rocket_final.parquet. Each step gives the commands or names the exact section that does. Two layers get built: the team stack (src/prc, whose gated prediction the strongest final member consumes as an expert) and the final members (pipeline/), which the blend and assembly layer (final/) turns into the submission.

challenge data + external archives
   │
   ├── team stack (src/prc, scripts/) ── gated run ── expert table ─┐
   │        steps 4 and 5                                           │
   └── feature matrix (pipeline/) ── final members (pipeline/) ─────┤
            step 6                        steps 7 and 8             │
                                                                    ▼
                         final/blend.py ── final/assemble.py ── final/verify.py
                                         step 9

Budget: the team stack and the final members are GPU work (one 48 GB card suffices; we used L40S and H200 nodes). The matrix builds, the expert table and everything in final/ run on CPU; per-step resource figures are in team stack reproduction §5.2.

docs.title: 1. Environment
docs.text:
git clone <repository URL> && cd <repository>
uv sync --group nn          # Python 3.12 and the locked packages, PyTorch included

uv installs Python 3.12 if it is missing; uv.lock pins every package. The GPU driver must support the CUDA version of the locked PyTorch wheels.

docs.title: 2. Challenge data
docs.text:
The organizers issue access keys to registered teams (data page). Keys never go into a file in the repository.

mc alias set prc https://s3.opensky-network.org <access-key> <secret-key>   # MinIO client, once
cp .env.example .env              # set PRC_TEAM_NAME; PRC_DATA_BUCKET is the organizers' bucket
uv run prc data pull              # mc mirror -> data/raw/
uv run prc data prepare           # -> data/interim/movements.parquet (team-stack input)

data/raw/ must end up holding the twelve training_2025-*.parquet files, ranking.parquet, final_ranking.parquet and final_submitting.parquet (data/README.md lists them).

docs.title: 3. External data
docs.text:
Download the EUROCONTROL arrival-ATFM workbook to data/external/Airport_Arrival_ATFM_Delay.xlsx (the link is in data/README.md §2). Every other external source is fetched by script, on a CPU machine with internet access (sources and licences):

uv run python scripts/fetch_external.py ourairports   # first: the ADS-B build reads runway thresholds
uv run python scripts/fetch_external.py metar --years 2025 2026
uv run python scripts/fetch_external.py osm
uv run python scripts/fetch_external.py xplane
uv run python scripts/fetch_external.py openmeteo
uv run python scripts/adsb_build.py run --stage 1 --workers 3   # ADS-B ground tracks, ~550 GB streamed
uv run python scripts/adsb_build.py run --stage 2 --workers 3
uv run python scripts/adsb_v2.py archive

These are the same commands as team stack reproduction §5.5, which also explains the two ADS-B archive states (110 early-2025 days are rebuilt from full traces partway through the chain).

docs.title: 4. The team stack
docs.text:
Follow team stack reproduction §5.6 to §5.14 exactly as written: feature cache, the member cells with three seeds each, seed merging, the routing flag, the traces rebuild, the no-flight-plan lane heads, the stamp mixture, the two cell stacks and the gate. The chain ends with the gated run outputs/runs/stack_l2_cell_ng4h2G_lt1h, which is the team-stack prediction everything below consumes. One extra member cell is needed here and is not part of §5.8: the set-attention variant the class model reads as an expert, trained and merged like any other cell (§5.7):

e=exp9004_setenc_overnight_extra
for s in 1 2 3; do
  uv run python scripts/run_cell.py --config "experiments/$e.yaml" --seed "$s" \
    --scheme month_loo --out "outputs/runs/loo-$e"
done
uv run python scripts/merge_seeds.py merge-seeds "outputs/runs/loo-$e"

docs.title: 5. The team-stack expert table
docs.text:
CPU only; run from the repository root after step 4 (and after the matrix of step 6, for the last command):

python pipeline/make_twins.py        # label-free arrival-twin table -> work/twins.parquet
python pipeline/team_base.py         # label-free projections of the gated stack -> work/v22_{oof,test}.parquet
python pipeline/team_corrector.py    # month-held residual corrector -> work/a14_*.parquet
python pipeline/team_dmodel.py       # month-held bounded-offset model -> work/a17_{oof,test}.parquet
python pipeline/team_table.py        # expert table -> work/v23_{oof,test}.parquet
python pipeline/team_adapt.py exp9004_setenc_overnight_extra__s1-2-3__month_loo t9004

Each script's docstring states what it fits and the pre-set rule under which a component is kept. The result is the expert table and the team_t9004 member tag that the class-structured combiner reads.

docs.title: 6. The final feature matrix
docs.text:
python pipeline/prepare_data.py     # input check + ATFM day table
python pipeline/strike_feats.py     # strike calendar -> work/strike_feats.parquet
python pipeline/fm_build.py         # raw-derived + ADS-B columns -> work/fm.parquet
FM_IN=work/fm.parquet FM_OUT=work/fm2.parquet python pipeline/fm_v2.py   # + ATFM columns

fm_build.py reads the per-departure ADS-B ground-track feature files from data/external/ (data/README.md §3); they are the adsb_ground and adsb_ground_v2 blocks built in step 3. The retrain matrix for the final months is the same build against the full submission set:

RANKING_FILE=final_ranking.parquet FM_OUT=work/fm_final.parquet python pipeline/fm_build.py
FM_IN=work/fm_final.parquet FM_OUT=work/fm2_final.parquet python pipeline/fm_v2.py

docs.title: 7. The final members
docs.text:
GPU. Train each member for folds 0 to 12 with the exact flags of the member table in pipeline/RUNS.md (also explained on the member pipeline page), in dependency order:

  1. gbm_v2 (its stage-1 cache is reused by every other GBM via S1TAG=v2), then gbm_v3a, gbm_vap3;
  2. the transformers ft_ftB7, ft_ftC7, ft_ftSC, ft_ftNE, ft_ftN10 and the auxiliary tags ft_ftB3, tr_trE, nn_nn2, gbm_hf10 (scripts and flags in the auxiliary-tags paragraph of pipeline/RUNS.md);
  3. gbm_eval.py with SAVE_MEMBERS=1 over the trained GBM tags, which writes the member-deviation tables, then the anomaly specialist gbm_anom1;
  4. the class models cm_cmA and cm_cmNA (they read the expert table of step 5 and every tag above).

For example, one member over all folds on a single GPU:

for FOLD in $(seq 0 12); do python pipeline/gbm_nested.py $FOLD --tag v2; done

or as a Slurm array (pipeline/jobs/py.sbatch, one fold per task). Every member writes work/<tag>/outer_NN.parquet.

docs.title: 8. The fold-0 retrains
docs.text: The months the primary members never predicted (February and June) are served by fold-0 retrains on the final matrix: rerun fold 0 of gbm_v2, gbm_v3a, gbm_vap3, ft_ftB7, ft_ftC7, ft_ftSC, ft_ftNE, ft_ftN10 with FM=work/fm2_final.parquet and the F-suffixed tags of pipeline/RUNS.md (transformers with 4 seeds). The class and anomaly models are deliberately not retrained; the final submission explains why.

docs.title: 9. Blend, assemble, verify
docs.text:
CPU, deterministic (blend and assembly):

python final/blend.py       # per-lane month-held simplex weights, blend OOF and test rows
python final/assemble.py    # corrections + label-free rules -> submissions/humble-rocket_final.parquet
python final/verify.py      # template check, per-month stats, sha256

docs.title: What "reproduced" means
docs.text: Given our member files, step 9 reproduces the submitted parquet byte for byte; the CPU steps are deterministic throughout. GPU training (steps 4, 7 and 8) is seeded but not bit-deterministic, so a full rebuild matches at seed- noise level rather than byte level; pipeline/RUNS.md carries the fidelity notes, and team stack reproduction §5.16 quantifies the equivalent statement for the team stack.

docs.title: Blend and assembly (final/)
docs.text:
final/ is the deterministic last layer: it reads the trained member outputs (work/<tag>/outer_NN.parquet, written by the member pipeline) and produces the submitted file. Given the member files, re-running it reproduces submissions/humble-rocket_final.parquet byte for byte.

python final/blend.py       # fit the per-lane weights, blend OOF and test rows
python final/assemble.py    # corrections + label-free rules -> the submission
python final/verify.py      # template check, per-month stats, sha256

All three run from the repository root and resolve paths from the environment:

Variable Default Used by WORK_DIR work member outputs and blend intermediates RAW_DIR data/raw challenge movement tables BLEND_DIR WORK_DIR where assemble.py finds the blend files RESULTS_DIR results the blend report SUBMISSIONS_DIR submissions the output parquet

docs.title: blend.py: per-lane month-held simplex blend
docs.text:
Members are combined per lane, four row populations with very different error structure:

Lane Rows nm_lt1h NM rows with C < 1 h (the bulk) nm_ge1h NM rows with C ≥ 1 h (long delays, heavy tail) nonm_lirf LIRF rows without an NM plan (smallest cell, largest per-row error) nonm_other no-NM rows elsewhere

Per lane, the weights solve non-negative least squares on the simplex (weights ≥ 0, summing to 1, lightly shrunk toward equal weights). They are fitted on the members' month-held 2025 out-of-fold predictions: the weights scored on month k are fitted on the other eleven months, so every 2025 month gets an honest read, and the rows of the never-evaluated submission months are leave-that-month-out estimates. Nothing in this layer sees 2026 labels.

Two member generations cover the submission rows (see the final submission): the primary members, whose fold 0 predicts the January/July rows, and the fold-0 retrains for the months the primary members never predicted. blend.py derives the retrain months from member coverage, fits one weight set per lane for each generation, and blends each submission row with the generation that covers its month. The class and anomaly models are excluded from the retrain-month member lists for the stacking-consistency reason the final-model page documents.

Outputs: work/blend_oof.parquet, work/blend_test.parquet, work/blend_weights.json and results/blend_report.txt (lane RMSEs, the fitted weights, the January+July read and the leave-February / leave-June reads).

docs.title: assemble.py: corrections, rules, writer
docs.text:
Steps, in order:

  1. read the blended submission rows;
  2. feeder-lateness correction: when the stand's feeding arrival went in-block more than 90 min behind schedule, the blend overshoots slightly. Offsets per C band are fitted on the 2025 out-of-fold blend with a heavy smoothing prior and validated month-held (negative in 8 of 12 months, interval below zero). Arrival block times are published for the submission months, so the trigger is computable on every 2026 row;
  3. LFPG EOBT-drift adjustment: in June and July 2026 the filed EOBT at LFPG sits about four minutes later relative to LOBT than in any 2025 month, a filing-practice change no 2025-trained model has seen. EOBT-anchored features mis-read exactly those rows; the EOBT-free transformer is immune by construction, so the mean gap between it and the base transformer over the affected cell estimates the bias, label-free. The gap is taken from the transformer pair of the generation that feeds each month's blend, and a diagnostic prints the same gap for every airport-month;
  4. label-free rules, proven on 2025: the window clip (on NM rows the label provably lies within ±3,620 s of MVT − LOBT), the rollover identity (when MVT − LOBT exceeds 20 h, LOBT kept the previous day's date and the label equals MVT − LOBT itself), and the twin cap (a no-NM departure whose matched arrival "twin" carries an NM plan must have fallen outside the join window, so y ≤ MVT − twin LOBT − 3606, applied when the bound is at least 300 s);
  5. floor at zero, round to Int32, write submissions/humble-rocket_final.parquet and validate it against the organizers' template.

docs.title: verify.py: submission checks
docs.text: Validates the written file against the organizers' template: row count, the two columns (MVT_ID_mvt, TAXITIME_SEC_mvt), Int32 type, no nulls, no negatives, the exact id set. It then prints per-month count, mean, median and p90, and the file's sha256.

docs.title: Package, CLI and scripts (src/prc, scripts/)
docs.text: The installable package prc and the scripts around it implement the team stack: data preparation, the content-addressed feature cache, the member experiments, and the post-processors whose end product the class-structured combiner consumes as an expert. The team stack method describes what these pieces compute; the reproduction guide runs them end to end. This page maps the code.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text: Path Content src/prc/ the package: data loading, feature blocks, models, CV, evaluation, the mixture post-processor, submission tools experiments/ one YAML per member experiment (model kind, feature blocks, target, CV scheme, seeds) scripts/ data fetchers and the post-processing chain (routing, lane head, mixture, stacker, gate) jobs/slurm/ Slurm templates for the team-stack stages pipeline/ the final members (member pipeline) final/ the blend and assembly layer (blend and assembly) assets/ the hand-compiled strike/disruption calendar data/ inputs, never committed; data/README.md says where each file comes from

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
uv sync --group nn    # Python 3.12, locked packages, PyTorch included

uv.lock pins every package. The prc command below is the package's console entry point (src/prc/cli.py); run it as uv run prc ....

docs.title: The prc command
docs.text:
Command What it does prc data pull mirror the challenge bucket into data/raw/ (mc mirror; keys come from the environment, never from a file) prc data prepare build data/interim/movements.parquet from the raw tables prc features list list the registered feature blocks and their cache state prc features build --all build the content-addressed feature cache prc train run one experiment YAML (one model, one CV scheme, one seed) prc status show a run's folds and metrics prc blend blend finished runs prc submit / prc upload write a submission file from a run; upload is explicit and separate prc registry the last N rows of the local experiment registry

Training at scale goes through scripts/run_cell.py (one experiment × one seed × all folds, resumable), which the Slurm template jobs/slurm/member-cell.sbatch wraps; see the reproduction guide.

docs.title: Package layout (src/prc/)
docs.text:
Module Content config.py typed experiment configuration (pydantic): model kind, feature blocks, target transform, CV scheme, test fit paths.py, runtime.py, cache.py repository paths, .env loading, GPU visibility, the content-addressed cache (block source hash × input hash × external-archive hash) data/ raw-table loading for training and ranking files features/ the feature blocks of the method page, one module per block, assembled through features/registry.py; no block reads the label or the off-block time of the row it describes cv/ fold assignment: month_loo, tail_nov_dec, month_jan_jul models/ the member architectures: CatBoost, LightGBM and XGBoost wrappers, RealMLP, GRU sequence encoder (seqenc.py), set-attention encoder (setenc.py), TabM, ModernNCA, plus the matrix cache shared by the neural models eval/ run directories, metrics, the experiment registry mixture/ the stamp-mixture building blocks used by scripts/mixture_v2.py: recording-class labels, per-class value expressions, feasibility masks blend/ run blending used by prc blend and scripts/blend_fit.py submit/ submission writing, validation and upload

Every experiment YAML in experiments/ names a model kind and a feature-block list; prc train resolves both through registries, so the YAML is the full definition of a member.

docs.title: Post-processing scripts
docs.text:
The chain after the members, in the order the reproduction guide runs it:

Script Role scripts/write_route_flag.py write the per-movement "has an ADS-B ground track" flag scripts/route_no_ground.py route rows without a ground track to a no-ADS-B twin member scripts/no_nm_lane_model.py the two-branch lane head on departures without a flight-plan record scripts/mixture_v2.py the six-class stamp mixture (build the frame, fit per run on GPU, apply) scripts/avg_runs.py average the predictions of two runs (used for the two fold-averaged mixture fits) scripts/stack_l2.py the cell stacker: non-negative member weights per airport × NM-record × C-band cell, shrunk toward parents scripts/gate_runs.py the gate on C: the final stack below 1 h, the earlier stack above scripts/write_candidate.py a submission-shaped candidate file, validated against the template; never uploads

Supporting tools:

Script Role scripts/fetch_external.py fetch the external archives (OurAirports, METAR, OSM, X-Plane Gateway, Open-Meteo), each with a sha256 manifest scripts/adsb_build.py, scripts/adsb_v2.py build the ADS-B ground-track archives from ADSB.lol releases scripts/run_cell.py, scripts/merge_seeds.py run one experiment cell; merge per-seed cells into one run with recomputed metrics scripts/stack_inner.py the 39 inner GRU runs and the stack table behind the exp0235 member scripts/paired_delta.py paired RMSE deltas between two runs with day-block bootstrap intervals, per row group (validation protocol) scripts/blend_fit.py, scripts/lane_report.py blend finished runs under the validation protocol; lane breakdown of a run scripts/delayed_flight_model.py, scripts/eda_no_nm_block_model.py post-processors over a finished run for delayed flights and the no-flight-plan lane scripts/adsb_pilot.py, scripts/adsb_pilot_phase2.py the pilot studies that established ADS-B ground tracks as a feature source

Every script prints its usage in its module docstring; the ones that take a run name read outputs/runs/<run>/ as written by prc train or scripts/run_cell.py.

docs.title: Member pipeline (pipeline/)
docs.text: pipeline/ holds the self-contained scripts that build the feature matrix and train every member behind the submitted file. Each script runs as a plain python call from the repository root; the GPU scripts also ran as Slurm array jobs with the generic templates in pipeline/jobs/ (one H200, 8 CPUs; jobs/py.sbatch <script> <args> or an --array=0-12 loop over the fold argument). pipeline/RUNS.md is the canonical record of every training run: the tag it wrote, and the flags that define it.

docs.title: Paths and environment variables
docs.text:
The scripts share pipeline/common.py, which resolves every path from the environment with these defaults:

Variable Default Meaning RAW_DIR data/raw challenge movement tables FEATURES_DIR data/external ADS-B ground-track feature files RANKING_FILE ranking.parquet the evaluation set joined as the test split RESULTS_DIR results text reports

Member outputs land under work/ (created on first use). common.py also carries the join-window constant W = 3606 (the verified maximum of |BLOCK − LOBT| over every 2025 departure with an NM record) and the shared loaders for the movement tables.

docs.title: The fold scheme
docs.text:
Every member is trained thirteen times:

  • folds 1 to 12: that 2025 month is held out and the member writes its out-of-fold prediction for it;
  • fold 0: the member fits on all twelve 2025 months and predicts the evaluation rows named by RANKING_FILE.

Each fold writes work/<tag>/outer_NN.parquet. The blend layer (final/) consumes these files by tag.

docs.title: Stage 0 and 1: inputs and the feature matrix
docs.text:
python pipeline/prepare_data.py                     # input check + ATFM day table
python pipeline/strike_feats.py                     # strike calendar -> work/strike_feats.parquet
python pipeline/fm_build.py                         # raw-derived + ADS-B columns -> work/fm.parquet
FM_IN=work/fm.parquet FM_OUT=work/fm2.parquet python pipeline/fm_v2.py   # + ATFM columns
  • prepare_data.py verifies the challenge tables and ADS-B feature files are in place (data/README.md lists where each one comes from) and converts the EUROCONTROL ATFM workbook to data/raw/apt_arr_atfm.parquet.
  • strike_feats.py turns assets/strike_calendar.csv (hand-compiled from public news sources) into per-departure strike and disruption features keyed by MVT_ID_mvt.
  • fm_build.py builds the departure feature matrix: the raw-derived blocks of newfeat.py (stand handover, arrival-default shares, NM-neighbour taxi, NM plan residual, day no-NM share), the ADS-B ground-track columns, and the LOBT-window and label-structure columns. The test split is whatever RANKING_FILE names.
  • fm_v2.py appends the EUROCONTROL daily airport-arrival ATFM delay features (airport × UTC date; open data; null means no regulation and maps to 0).

The retrain matrix for the final months is the same build against the full submission set:

RANKING_FILE=final_ranking.parquet FM_OUT=work/fm_final.parquet python pipeline/fm_build.py
FM_IN=work/fm_final.parquet FM_OUT=work/fm2_final.parquet python pipeline/fm_v2.py

docs.title: Stage 2 and 3: the member scripts
docs.text: Three model families, all run per fold (python pipeline/<script>.py $FOLD --tag <tag> [flags]):

docs.title: Two-stage GBM: gbm_nested.py
docs.text:
Nested two-stage GPU XGBoost on the full matrix. Stage 1 predicts properties of the off-block stamp, fitted with inner month-held folds over the training months so no stage-2 training row sees an in-fold stage-1 fit:

Stage-1 output Meaning d_hat mean of d = BLOCK − LOBT (NM rows; bounded ±3606) dq10/50/90 quantiles of d, giving predicted bounds on the label p_def P(|BLOCK − SCHED| ≤ 10 s), the schedule-default probability p_gt1h P(label > 1 h and not a schedule default)

Stage 2 fits the taxi time: y_base (no stage-1 features), y_s1 (with them), and the mixture y_mix = p_def · C + (1 − p_def) · normal-model. Variants are selected with --cfg (and reuse a tagged stage-1 cache via S1TAG): a CatBoost mixture, the mixture fitted per airport, and a four-class stamp specialist that sees the other members' disagreement as features (work/members_oof.parquet / members_test.parquet, written by gbm_eval.py with SAVE_MEMBERS=1).

docs.title: Distributional FT-transformer: ftdist.py
docs.text: A feature-token transformer (after Gorishniy et al. 2021) whose head is one softmax over taxi-time bins masked to the NM join window, plus a point mass at y = C masked where a schedule default is impossible. Targets are Gaussian-smoothed histograms (HL-Gauss); the prediction is the distribution mean, the squared-error optimum. The loss is cross-entropy plus a small MSE term on the mean. Rollover rows are left out of training, as for every member. Variants come from flags: --s1 v2 adds the nested stage-1 outputs as extra tokens, --strikes adds the strike-calendar flags, --drop eobt1,arvt1,=me removes every feature anchored on the filed EOBT (the EOBT-free variant), --w-nonm 10 upweights the no-flight-plan rows.

docs.title: Class-structured combiner: class_mix.py
docs.text:
The strongest single member combines member components instead of final predictions:

ŷ = p_def·C + p_near·(C − offset) + p_long·v_long + p_normal·Σ_j g_j·n_j

One MLP outputs the class probabilities (the default class masked where infeasible), the gate g over the members' conditional normal means n_j, and small bounded corrections, from every member's class signals: the transformer's p_def, the GBM stage-1 p_def and p_gt1h, the anomaly specialist's class probabilities and long-stamp value, the bounded offset model, the team stack's prediction, and context features. The loss is MSE plus a class log-loss on the observed recording class. --lane nonm trains a second instance on the no-flight-plan rows only.

docs.title: The trained members
docs.text:
From pipeline/RUNS.md (the primary runs; FM=work/fm2.parquet):

Tag Script and flags What it is gbm_v2 gbm_nested.py $FOLD --tag v2 two-stage XGBoost: nested stage-1 stamp models, then y_base/y_s1/y_mix gbm_v3a S1TAG=v2 gbm_nested.py $FOLD --tag v3a --only-cat --cfg cat_d10s1,catmix CatBoost mixture (y_catmix) + plain deep CatBoost gbm_vap3 S1TAG=v2 gbm_nested.py $FOLD --tag vap3 --only-cat --cfg catmixapy_s201 the mixture fitted per airport gbm_anom1 S1TAG=v2 gbm_nested.py $FOLD --tag anom1 --only-cat --cfg anom_s1 four-class stamp specialist over member deviations ft_ftB7 ftdist.py $FOLD --tag ftB7 --seeds 0..6 distributional transformer, 7 seeds ft_ftC7 ftdist.py $FOLD --tag ftC7 --seeds 0..6 --s1 v2 with stage-1 outputs as extra tokens ft_ftSC ftdist.py $FOLD --tag ftSC --seeds 0,1,2 --strikes work/strike_feats.parquet strike-calendar tokens ft_ftNE ftdist.py $FOLD --tag ftNE --seeds 1..18 --drop eobt1,arvt1,=me EOBT-free variant ft_ftNE4 first four seeds of ft_ftNE, merged 4-seed average for the long-delay lane ft_ftN10 ftdist.py $FOLD --tag ftN10 --seeds 0..9 --w-nonm 10 no-flight-plan rows upweighted cm_cmA class_mix.py --tag cmA --more --plus --seeds 0..16 class-structured combiner, 17 seeds cm_cmNA class_mix.py --tag cmNA --lane nonm --seeds 0..44 the no-flight-plan instance, 45 seeds

Fold-0 retrains for the final months (gbm_v2F, gbm_v3aF, gbm_vap3F, ft_ftCF, ft_ftNEFF, ft_ftB7F, ft_ftSCF, ft_ftN10F) use the same flags against the retrain matrix, fold 0 only, transformers with 4 seeds. No retrain exists for the class and anomaly models; the final-model page explains why they are excluded on the retrain months.

Auxiliary tags consumed by cm_cmA as inputs (not blend members): ft_ftB3 (3-seed base transformer), tr_trE (tabr.py, a retrieval-augmented network in the TabR style), nn_nn2 (nn_mix.py, a window-bounded neural mixture), gbm_hf10 (gbm_nested.py --cfg catmixd_json with trial 10 of hpo_trials.json), and team_t9004 (the team member experiments/exp9004_setenc_overnight_extra.yaml, converted by team_adapt.py).

docs.title: The team-stack expert table
docs.text:
The class-structured combiner reads the team stack's prediction as one of its experts. Five CPU scripts turn the gated team-stack run (outputs/runs/stack_l2_cell_ng4h2G_lt1h, the end of the team stack reproduction) into the table and tag the combiner consumes; the ordered commands are in reproducing the submission and in pipeline/RUNS.md:

Script What it does make_twins.py the label-free arrival-twin table (work/twins.parquet) team_base.py label-free projections of the gated stack: window clip, in-window model, rollover identity, twin cap, a LIRF offset (work/v22_{oof,test}.parquet) team_corrector.py a month-held residual corrector with stand-handover and arrival-stamp features the members do not see directly (work/a14_*.parquet) team_dmodel.py a month-held model of the bounded off-block offset d = BLOCK − LOBT on NM rows (work/a17_{oof,test}.parquet) team_table.py the expert table: the base plus each corrector that passes its pre-set month-held rule (work/v23_{oof,test}.parquet) team_adapt.py converts a team run directory into a member tag (work/team_<short>/outer_NN.parquet)

gbm_eval.py TAG [extra_tags...] scores nested member outputs against the expert table and stacks them with it, per lane, month-held; with SAVE_MEMBERS=1 it writes the member-deviation tables the anomaly specialist reads.

docs.title: Reproduction notes
docs.text: The table above reconstructs each run's flags from the scripts' defaults and our run records; the full argv of every historical run was not retained, and retraining a GPU member reproduces its predictions only up to hardware nondeterminism. The blend and assembly layer (final/) is exactly deterministic given the member files: re-running it reproduces the submitted parquet byte for byte.
